answer: Each PoA challenge is derived from a future drand quicknet pulse, whose threshold-BLS signature is publicly verifiable and unpredictable before release. Agents commit to responses before the reveal window closes; the pulse then binds the challenge to that commitment, making cached answers and offline farming by automated sybil swarms ineffective. Randomness alone does not prove unique identity, so participation limits or resource costs must constrain repeated attempts—whether an agent names its node oasis, reef, or fable.
